problem: Object-level semantic mapping for quadrupeds often relies on heavy 3D fusion or open-vocabulary/vision-language scoring loops that raise latency and power draw, and purely geometric maps cannot support object-goal tasks like 'go to the toolbox'.
motivation: Navigation goals are often tied to objects rather than coordinates, so planners need a queryable object layer. Real quadruped deployments have limited onboard compute, so a lightweight mapping substrate is needed.
key_idea: Project YOLOv11 RGB-D detections into a 2D SLAM Toolbox occupancy map and maintain persistent object instances via map-frame nearest-neighbor association with short-term and long-term memory.
insight: Simple Euclidean association plus a promotion gate (short-term buffer to long-term list after repeated sightings) is enough to keep object instances stable across viewpoint changes without duplicates. Evidence is only qualitative (one lab run, demo video), with no ablations. The authors note that D435 depth is inconsistent with the LiDAR scan plane, causing range/pose bias.
method: 2D mapping: SLAM Toolbox builds an online occupancy map from a 2D LiDAR, using T265 visual-inertial odometry as a motion prior with scan matching and loop closure.

Detection: YOLOv11 on D435 RGB frames yields class, score and 2D boxes after NMS. Aligned depth gives a 3D position, which is transformed into the map frame via calibrated extrinsics and the SLAM pose.
Map projection: z is set to 0 and only yaw is kept, giving 2D object positions. Per-class confidence cutoff is 0.65.
Same-frame merge: near-duplicate detections of the same class within 0.20 m are reduced to the highest-score one.
Long-term association: a detection within 0.80 m of a confirmed same-class object (nearest-neighbor search) increments its hit count and leaves its stored pose unchanged.
Short-term buffer and promotion: unmatched detections update or create short-term records. A record is promoted to long-term after a gate of 10 hits / 2.0 s / 0.50 mean confidence.
Output: confirmed objects (class, pose, confidence) are published in the map frame, integrated with the occupancy map and readable by a planner.

setting.backbone: YOLOv11 (pretrained detector, used as-is) + SLAM Toolbox; heuristic association
setting.training_data: none (pretrained YOLOv11 used off the shelf; no training reported)
setting.observation: RGB-D (RealSense D435) + 2D LiDAR + T265 visual-inertial odometry
setting.action_space: none (mapping only; robot teleoperated by joystick)

numbers_note: No quantitative metrics reported; only a qualitative on-robot demo (lab with two people and two chairs) and topic frame-rate plots.
results: On a Spot robot in a lab, the mapper produced stable persistent instances of person and chair in real time, suppressing per-frame duplicates and keeping objects when out of view. No quantitative comparison or benchmark is reported.
limitations: Depth misalignment between the D435 and the LiDAR scan plane biases object placement.
Association is purely geometric (no appearance cues) and relies on detector box centers; the map is 2D.
Evaluation is qualitative, indoor-only, and covers only two classes; no autonomous navigation using the layer.
